trace.code: ssh_auth_agent_read() reads a 32-bit packet `length` from the untrusted agent channel and checks `buffer_length >= length+4` (uint32 wrap bypassable) before dispatching.

SSH2_AGENT_SIGN_REQUEST handler sets pos = buffer+5 and calls buffer_read_string(&pos, &key_blob_length) then sign_data = buffer_read_string(&pos, &sign_data_length) — neither length is validated against the remaining buffer.
guac_common_ssh_buffer_read_string() reads a 32-bit length and advances the pointer by it with NO bounds check (*buffer += *length), returning a pointer into (or past) the buffer.
ssh_auth_agent_sign(auth_agent, sign_data, sign_data_length) signs sign_data_length bytes from the out-of-bounds sign_data pointer.

preconditions: a user connects to a malicious (or compromised) SSH server through Guacamole
SSH agent forwarding is enabled for the connection (so the server can open an agent channel)
the server sends an SSH2_AGENT_SIGN_REQUEST packet with an oversized key_blob_length

evidence.vulnerable_version: guacamole-server @ bb1ba8e (current master; SSH agent forwarding)
evidence.fixed_version: proposed: bound string length against remaining buffer
evidence.observed_result: A crafted SSH agent SIGN_REQUEST with key_blob_length=0x7FFFFFFF advances the read pointer ~2 GB past the 4096-byte auth_agent->buffer; the subsequent buffer_read_string and ssh_key_sign dereference heap far out of bounds (tracked read at offset 2147483656, buffer size 4096). The fixed reader rejects the oversized key_blob_length before any out-of-bounds access. NOTE: the OOB bytes only feed SHA-1 + a signature (no confidentiality leak), and guacd forks a per-connection child, so the crash is limited to the attacker's own session — hence LOW (C:N/I:N/A:L), not HIGH.

real_exploit.target: apache/guacamole-server src/protocols/ssh/ssh_agent.c (ssh_auth_agent_handle_packet/read) + src/common-ssh/buffer.c (guac_common_ssh_buffer_read_string) @ bb1ba8e — verbatim unbounded length-prefixed string reader
real_exploit.backend: a faithful C reimplementation of the vulnerable read path against a tracked 4096-byte agent buffer (canary + bounds-tracking detects any read past the buffer), driven by a crafted SSH2_AGENT_SIGN_REQUEST packet
real_exploit.demonstrated: Vulnerable: key_blob_length=0x7FFFFFFF pushes the pointer ~2 GB past the 4096-byte buffer and the next read/sign dereference that offset (OOB read detected). Fixed: oversized key_blob_length is rejected. Heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) demonstrated against the real unbounded reader.
